name: Customer Terms and Conditions
terms:
CareYogi is committed to delivering excellence in healthcare services, prioritizing patient-centered care, innovative technology-driven processes, and optimal clinical outcomes. Patient and family cooperation is crucial to achieving our mission. Please review this agreement carefully, as it outlines the understanding between you ('Patient') and CareYogi ('Agency') regarding the requested services. Our authorized representative can provide clarifications on the agreement's contents.


Service Details:

a. The CareYogi representative has thoroughly explained the services to the Patient's Next of Kin (NOK).

b. Clear distinctions between different service categories and their deliverables have been provided.

c. Shift timings are confirmed as agreed upon during the onboarding process.

d. Each admission at CareYogi involves a standard care assessment, support, and supervisory visits according to protocols.

e. Staff assignments are based on care requirements, covering assigned staff's days off and emergency leaves; replacements are allocated based on availability.

f. In unavoidable situations, services may be temporarily suspended until alternative arrangements are made.

g. Services will be rendered as per advance booking and the service agreement.


Payment Terms:

a. Advance payment of estimated charges and recurring deposits for subsequent service cycles are required.

b. Additional charges apply if the same staff continues during their off days, leaves, or public holidays.

c. Service costs may vary based on changing care requirements due to the patient's condition.

d. Additional charges apply for consumables used during care.

e. Transportation charges vary if the patient requires staff accompaniment to different locations.

f. The family assumes responsibility for any injuries sustained by staff during service.


General Terms and Conditions:

  1. Effective from the signing date for one year or until services are availed, whichever is earlier.
  2. No direct cash payments to staff unless authorized.
  3. Professional service fees include applicable taxes but exclude GST.
  4. Services are strictly as agreed upon; any changes require written agreement.
  5. Basic amenities for staff at the beneficiary's premises are the beneficiary's responsibility.
  6. Staff will not perform domestic chores.
  7. Respectful treatment of staff is expected from the beneficiary and family members.
  8. Staff entitlements under labor laws include leave provisions.
  9. Staff replacements may occur with notice; unsuitable replacements will be addressed promptly.
  10. Termination with notice or mutual consent; immediate termination for material breach.
  11. Financial settlements upon termination; no refunds upon death or relocation.
  12. Non-solicitation clause post-termination; breach may incur penalties.
  13. Governed by Indian law; disputes resolved in New Delhi courts.


Service-Specific Terms:

a. Acceptance of inherent risks by the beneficiary in receiving services.

b. Limitation of liability for infection, injury, or death during service provision.

c. Indemnification of CareYogi by the beneficiary for claims arising from service-related incidents.


Feedback and Contact:

For concerns, feedback, suggestions, or complaints regarding care or services, contact our Service Excellence Desk at info@careyogis.com or call

9810918237.


Consent:

By continuing to use our website and/or mobile app, you acknowledge understanding and agreement with the above terms and conditions.

terms:
IMPORTANT CUSTOMER NOTICE

Please read this Agreement before accepting a CareYogi service. Healthcare involves clinical judgment and cannot

guarantee a particular diagnosis, treatment response or outcome. If a healthcare professional considers that your

condition requires a higher level of care, you may be advised to attend a hospital, emergency facility, or other

appropriate provider.

If you believe you are experiencing a medical emergency, do not wait for a CareYogi appointment or

teleconsultation. Seek immediate emergency medical assistance.

If you have availed Emergency Assistance Service from CareYogi, emergency limitations are governed by the

separate CareYogi Emergency and Safety Acknowledgement.

1. PARTIES AND DEFINITIONS

1.1 Company. “CareYogi”, “we”, “us” or “Company” means Mriduvandan Health Tech Private Limited, doing business

under CareYogi trademarked brand and operating the CareYogi Digital Hospital platform.

Registered/Corporate Address: 5th Floor, Adilakshmi Square, Plot No 137, Old Mumbai Highway, Gachibowli,

Hyderabad, Telangana 500032

Customer Support:  9810918237

Email: info@careyogis.com

Website: https://www.careyogis.com.

Grievance Officer: Rohit Madhusudan, Chief Operating Officer, email: RohitM@careyogis.com, Ph: 9810614737

1.2 Platform. “Platform” means the CareYogi website, mobile applications, APIs, databases, software, user interfaces,

communication systems and other digital interfaces operated or authorised by CareYogi.

1.3 Customer. “Customer” means the individual who creates an account, purchases or arranges a service, or

otherwise accepts this Agreement.

1.4 Patient. “Patient” or “Beneficiary” means the person for whom healthcare or related services are requested or

delivered. Customer and Patient may be the same person or different persons. Customer may serve as Authorized

Representative and primary or secondary contact for the Patient.

1.5 Authorised Representative. A parent, legal guardian, caregiver or any other person legally authorized to act for

the Patient.

1.6 Healthcare Professional. A doctor/RMP, nurse, physiotherapist, therapist or other appropriately qualified

professional legally permitted to provide the relevant service.

1.7 Service Provider. A Healthcare Professional, clinic, hospital, diagnostic centre, pharmacy, rehabilitation provider,

home-care provider, medical-equipment provider or other third party providing a service through or in connection

with CareYogi.

1.8 Services. Teleconsultation, in-clinic consultation, doctor home visits, nursing and home healthcare,

physiotherapy and rehabilitation, speech and hearing therapy, diagnostics, medication/pharmacy services, wellness

and nutrition support, digital health records, care coordination and other services made available from time to time.


2. ACCEPTANCE, ELIGIBILITY AND AUTHORITY

2.1 By selecting “I Agree”, “Accept & Continue”, “Book & Accept”, or an equivalent affirmative electronic action, you

agree to be bound by this Agreement for the services you use or purchase.

2.2 You confirm that you are at least 18 years old, or are the parent, guardian or other person legally authorised to

accept this Agreement and applicable consents for the Patient.

2.3 If you arrange services for another Patient, you confirm that the information you provide is accurate and that you

have the required authority.

2.4 You must promptly update material changes to contact information, Patient information and emergency-contact

information.


3. NATURE AND SCOPE OF CAREYOGI SERVICES

3.1 CareYogi is a technology-enabled healthcare platform. Depending on the service, CareYogi may provide a service

directly through its own personnel or facilitate a service delivered by an independent Service Provider. The

responsible Healthcare Professional or Service Provider will be identified or communicated where applicable.

•Physician consultations through video, in-clinic interaction or home visits.

•Consultations/services across applicable systems of medicine and allied healthcare disciplines.

•Home healthcare, skilled nursing, assisted daily living and care coordination.

•Physiotherapy, rehabilitation and other therapy services.

•Medication management and pharmacy/medicine fulfilment.

•Diagnostic investigations and sample collection.

•Wellness, nutrition and preventive-health services.

•Digital health records and care-coordination functionality.

•Subscription or membership programmes.

3.2 Availability depends on clinical appropriateness, professional availability, geography, operating hours,

infrastructure, applicable law, and reasonable operational requirements.

3.3 CareYogi does not promise that every requested service or particular professional will be available at every

requested time.


4. CAREYOGI'S ROLE AND CLINICAL RESPONSIBILITY

4.1 Healthcare Professionals are responsible for their professional clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment

recommendations, prescriptions and other clinical decisions within their lawful scope.

4.2 CareYogi may perform onboarding, identity, registration, qualification or other verification checks using

information supplied by providers and/or relevant registries, councils, institutions or other sources. “Verified” status

is not a guarantee of clinical outcome or professional performance.

4.3 CareYogi does not direct or control the independent clinical judgment of a Healthcare Professional.

4.4 Nothing in this Agreement excludes or limits responsibility or liability of CareYogi that cannot lawfully be

excluded or limited.

4.5 Where a third-party provider independently delivers healthcare, that provider remains responsible for its

professional services to the extent provided by applicable law and the relevant contractual arrangement.


5. GENERAL HEALTHCARE SERVICES CONSENT

5.1 You voluntarily request and consent to receive the healthcare or related services you select through CareYogi,

subject to the specific consent applicable to the service.

5.2 You understand that healthcare involves uncertainty and no diagnosis, treatment response, recovery period or

clinical outcome can be guaranteed.

5.3 You understand that a Healthcare Professional may request additional information, examinations, investigations

or an in-person assessment before making a clinical decision.

5.4 You understand that a Healthcare Professional may decline, modify or stop a requested service or recommend

escalation where clinically indicated.

5.5 You may refuse or discontinue a service, subject to applicable law and the clinical circumstances.

5.6 You agree to provide accurate and complete information reasonably relevant to my care, including symptoms,

history, allergies, medicines and investigations.

5.7 You agree to follow reasonable instructions provided by the responsible Healthcare Professional and promptly

communicate material deterioration or new symptoms.


6. PATIENT AND CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES

•Provide accurate identity, contact, medical and service information.

•Disclose relevant allergies, medicines and significant medical conditions.

•Provide reasonable access to the Patient, premises, equipment or records required for the booked service.

•For home services, maintain a reasonably safe and accessible environment and disclose known hazards.

•Treat Healthcare Professionals and CareYogi personnel respectfully and not engage in violence, threats,

harassment or discriminatory conduct.

•Use prescriptions, medicines, devices and healthcare products only for legitimate and lawful purposes.

•Keep account credentials and authentication information secure.

•Provide and maintain an emergency contact where requested.


7. TELECONSULTATION AND REMOTE CARE CONSENT

This section applies whenever healthcare is delivered through video, audio, chat, mobile application, connected

device or other remote technology. If you are taking CareYogi service through teleconsultation or other remote

means,

7.1 You understand and consent to healthcare being delivered through telemedicine or other remote means where

clinically appropriate.

7.2 You understand that the Healthcare Professional may request additional information, photographs, reports,

measurements or an in-person visit where necessary.

7.3 You understand that connectivity failures, device problems, audio/video quality and other technical limitations

can affect remote care.

7.4 You agree to use a reasonably private environment and to inform the Healthcare Professional if another person

is present where relevant.

7.5 You understand that a prescription or treatment recommendation may not be issued remotely where

inappropriate or prohibited.

7.6 Where a prescription or clinical document is generated electronically, the responsible Healthcare Professional

remains responsible for its clinical content and final approval.


8. IN-CLINIC CONSULTATION CONSENT

If you have opted for in-clinic consultation,

8.1 You consent to the selected in-clinic consultation/service.

8.2 you understand that the clinic/hospital may have additional operational policies and service-specific consent

forms.

8.3 Acceptance of this Agreement does not constitute blanket consent to every future medical procedure; additional

informed consent may be required.


9. DOCTOR HOME VISIT AND HOME HEALTHCARE CONSENT

If you have opted for a Practitioner Home Visit or Healthcare Services at Home,

9.1 You consent to the Healthcare Professional and authorised service personnel entering the designated location

for the booked service.

9.2 You understand that the home environment may limit examination, diagnostics, equipment or treatment

options.

9.3 You will disclose known hazards, infectious risks, accessibility limitations or other circumstances affecting safe

service delivery.

9.4 If the professional considers the home setting clinically inadequate or unsafe, the service may be modified,

stopped or escalated.

9.5 I understand that home healthcare is not hospital-equivalent care and may require escalation if the Patient's

condition changes.


10. NURSING, CAREGIVER AND ASSISTED DAILY LIVING (ADL) SERVICES

If you have booked Nursing or ADL services,

10.1 Nursing services will be provided according to the service booked and the professional's lawful scope.

10.2 Assisted daily living/caregiver services are not a substitute for skilled medical care unless expressly stated.

10.3 A change in the Patient's condition may require reassessment by a nurse, doctor or other appropriate

professional.

10.4 Services may be modified or stopped where staff safety, Patient safety, clinical appropriateness or legal

requirements make continued service unsuitable.


11. PHYSIOTHERAPY, SPEECH THERAPY AND REHABILITATION CONSENT

11.1 You consent to assessment and therapy appropriate to the service booked.

11.2 You understand that physical activity, exercise and mobilisation may involve ordinary risks such as temporary

pain, fatigue, dizziness, strain or injury.

11.3 You will inform the therapist of relevant medical conditions, recent surgery, falls, pregnancy where relevant, or

other factors affecting safe treatment.

11.4 The therapist may modify, postpone or stop treatment if it is considered unsafe.


12. DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES

If you opt for Pathology or Diagnostic services with CareYogi

12.1 You consent to the selected diagnostic investigation/sample collection.

12.2 You understand ordinary risks associated with specimen collection, where applicable.

12.3 You understand that results should be interpreted in clinical context by an appropriately qualified professional.

12.4 Responsibility for testing and reporting lies within the professional scope of The diagnostic provider.


13. MEDICINES, PRESCRIPTIONS AND PHARMACY SERVICES

13.1 Prescriptions, where issued, are determined by the responsible prescribing professional subject to applicable

law.

13.2 CareYogi may facilitate pharmacy or medicine fulfilment through an authorised provider.

13.3 You will not misuse, resell or unlawfully transfer medicines or prescriptions.

13.4 Uploaded prescriptions may be transcribed or structured administratively, but final clinical approval remains

with the prescribing or authorized medical professional.

13.5 Product-specific statutory responsibilities may rest with the manufacturer, importer, pharmacy or other

responsible entity as required by law.


14. DIGITAL HEALTH RECORDS AND ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS

14.1 You consent to receiving service-related communications electronically, including appointments, clinical

documents, prescriptions, reports and care-plan information.

14.2 CareYogi may create, maintain or make available digital health records associated with services delivered

through the Platform, subject to the separate Privacy Policy and applicable law.

14.3 You understand that electronic systems can experience interruptions or transmission errors.

14.4 Clinical records remain subject to applicable professional and legal record-keeping requirements.


15. FAMILY MEMBER, CAREGIVER AND AUTHORISED REPRESENTATIVE ACCESS

15.1 A Patient may designate a family member, caregiver or other authorised person to receive specified service or

care information where supported.

15.2 Access may be limited by role, purpose or information category.

15.3 CareYogi may disclose information where required or permitted by law or necessary for urgent patient safety,

subject to applicable requirements.

15.4 Privacy and personal-data processing are governed by the separate Privacy Policy.


16. APPOINTMENTS, CANCELLATION AND SERVICE AVAILABILITY

16.1 Appointment times are subject to availability and applicable cancellation policy.

16.2 If a provider cancels or is unavailable, CareYogi may offer rescheduling, an alternative provider or refund/credit

where applicable.

16.3 No-show, late-arrival, cancellation and refund rules will be displayed before booking or otherwise

communicated.

16.4 Clinical urgency does not guarantee appointment availability.


17. FEES, PAYMENT, REFUNDS AND TAXES

17.1 Price, taxes, applicable platform/service charges and total payable will be displayed before purchase where

reasonably practicable.

17.2 Payment may be processed by CareYogi or an authorised payment provider.

17.3 Refunds, credits and cancellation charges are governed by the applicable service or subscription policy.

17.4 The Customer remains responsible for amounts properly due for services delivered, subject to applicable law

and the stated refund policy.


18. SUBSCRIPTIONS AND CARE PROGRAMMES

18.1 Each programme will identify inclusions, exclusions, duration, fees, renewal arrangements, service limits and

cancellation/refund rules.

18.2 A subscription does not guarantee a particular clinical outcome, provider, appointment time, hospital admission

or availability of a particular service unless expressly stated.


19. CLINICAL ESCALATION AND REFERRAL

19.1 Where a professional considers that the Patient needs a higher level of care, CareYogi may recommend or

facilitate escalation to a hospital, emergency facility, specialist or other appropriate provider.

19.2 Such recommendation supports patient safety but does not guarantee availability, admission, treatment or

outcome at the receiving facility.

19.3 Emergency response, ambulance or emergency-facility services are subject to the separate Emergency & Safety

Acknowledgement and relevant provider terms.


20. SERVICE PROVIDER INFORMATION

20.1 Where applicable, CareYogi will display or communicate the identity and relevant professional information of

the provider responsible for the booked service.

20.2 Information may include name, professional category, specialty and registration information where required or

permitted.

20.3 Display of provider information does not guarantee a clinical outcome.


21. PRIVACY AND PERSONAL DATA

21.1 Personal data and health-related information are processed under CareYogi's separate Privacy Policy and

applicable law. The Privacy Policy describes categories of data, purposes, disclosures, retention and available

rights/mechanisms. Nothing in this Agreement replaces the Privacy Policy or converts all data processing into

blanket healthcare consent.


22. ELECTRONIC ACCEPTANCE AND RECORD OF CONSENT

22.1 This Agreement may be accepted by checkbox, button, OTP-authenticated action, digital signature or another

approved electronic mechanism.

22.2 CareYogi may retain an electronic audit trail showing Agreement version, date/time, account identifier, consent

type and other technical information reasonably necessary to evidence acceptance, subject to applicable law and

the Privacy Notice.

22.3 Service-specific consent is captured when the relevant service is requested. Acceptance of the Master

Agreement is not intended as blanket informed consent to every future medical procedure.

22.4 The accepted version and applicable consent records may be made available through the Platform or another

appropriate channel.


23. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND PLATFORM USE

The Platform, software, branding, content, design and proprietary materials are owned by or licensed to CareYogi.

Customers may use the Platform only for lawful, authorised healthcare purposes and may not copy, reverse

engineer, misuse or commercially exploit it except as permitted by law.


24. PLATFORM AVAILABILITY AND THIRD-PARTY TECHNOLOGY

24.1 CareYogi will use reasonable efforts to maintain the Platform but does not promise uninterrupted availability.

24.2 Remote services may depend on telecommunications networks, devices, cloud services and other third-party

technology.

24.3 CareYogi may suspend or modify Platform functionality for maintenance, security, safety, legal compliance or

other reasonable operational purposes.


25. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

25.1 Nothing in this Agreement limits liability or responsibility to the extent prohibited by applicable law.

25.2 CareYogi is responsible for its own contractual obligations and services it directly undertakes to provide.

25.3 For independently delivered third-party professional services, the responsible Service Provider remains

responsible for its professional acts and omissions to the extent provided by law and the relevant arrangement.

25.4 CareYogi does not guarantee clinical outcomes, recovery, diagnosis, treatment response, hospital admission or

uninterrupted access to a particular provider.

25.5 Any service-specific limitation must be consistent with applicable consumer and healthcare law.


26. COMPLAINTS AND GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL

26.1 Customers may raise service, clinical, billing, provider, safety or platform complaints through CareYogi support

channels.

26.2 CareYogi will maintain an appropriate grievance mechanism and publish required contact details.

26.3 Clinical complaints may be reviewed with the responsible professional/provider in accordance with applicable

law.

26.4 Privacy/data complaints may also be raised using the Privacy Notice contact mechanism.

27. SUSPENSION OR TERMINATION

The Customer may stop using the Platform subject to outstanding payments, active services, subscriptions and law.

CareYogi may suspend or terminate access where reasonably necessary for safety, fraud prevention, non-payment,

misuse, unlawful activity, staff abuse, security, legal compliance or material breach. Termination does not affect

rights or obligations that should survive.

28. CHANGES TO THIS AGREEMENT

CareYogi may update this Agreement. The revised version will identify its effective date. Where a change materially

affects Customer rights or obligations, CareYogi will provide notice and, where required by law, obtain fresh

acceptance before the affected service continues. Continued use will not by itself be treated as acceptance of a

material change where affirmative acceptance is legally required.

29. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

This Agreement is governed by the laws applicable in India. Subject to mandatory statutory rights, disputes may be

subject to the jurisdiction of courts at [Hyderabad, Telangana / other agreed jurisdiction]. Nothing prevents a

Customer from exercising a statutory right to approach a competent consumer, regulatory, judicial or other

authority.

30. GENERAL

If any provision is invalid or unenforceable, it will be modified or severed to the minimum extent necessary and the

remainder continues.

Failure to enforce a provision immediately does not waive the right to enforce it later.

Neither party is responsible for delay caused by circumstances beyond reasonable control, subject to applicable law.

This Agreement, the separate Privacy Notice, separate Emergency & Safety Acknowledgement, applicable service

policies and any additional provider/procedure consent form accepted for a particular service form the relevant

CareYogi customer framework.

CAREYOGI DIGITAL HOSPITAL


PRIVACY POLICY & PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION NOTICE

Version: v1.0    Effective Date: Aug 15th, 2026    Last Updated: Aug 14th, 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how CareYogi Digital Hospital collects, uses, stores, shares and otherwise processes

personal data when you use the CareYogi website, mobile application, digital-health services, teleconsultation, in-

clinic services, home healthcare, care-coordination services and related products and services.

This Policy is intended to operate alongside the CareYogi Master Customer Agreement, Healthcare Services Consent

and Service-Specific Consents. It is not a substitute for clinical informed consent, emergency acknowledgement, or

any consent required for a particular medical procedure.


1. WHO WE ARE

CareYogi, operated by Mriduvandan Health Tech Private Limited (“CareYogi”, “we”, “us” or “our”), is a technology-

enabled healthcare platform. Depending on the service, CareYogi may provide services directly or facilitate services

delivered by independent healthcare professionals, hospitals, clinics, laboratories, pharmacies, home-care providers,

therapists and other authorised Service Providers.

Registered/Corporate Address: 5th Floor, Adilakshmi Square, Plot No 137, Old Mumbai Highway, Gachibowli,

Hyderabad, Telangana 500032

Customer Support:  9810918237

Email: info@careyogis.com

Website: https://www.careyogis.com.

Privacy Contact / Person responsible for privacy queries: Satyendra Kumar Sinha, Chief Executive Officer, email:

satyendras@careyogis.com, Phone: 9885193111

Grievance Officer: Rohit Madhusudan, Chief Operating Officer, email: RohitM@careyogis.com, Ph: 9810614737

For a particular healthcare service, the relevant Service Provider may also process personal data under its own

professional, legal and contractual responsibilities. Where appropriate, CareYogi will identify or communicate the

relevant provider.

2. SCOPE OF THIS POLICY

This Policy applies to personal data collected or otherwise processed through:

•CareYogi websites, web portals and mobile applications.

•Teleconsultation, video, audio, chat and remote-care services.

•In-clinic consultations and services arranged through CareYogi.

•Doctor home visits and home healthcare, nursing, caregiver and therapy services.

•Diagnostic investigations, sample collection and laboratory-related services.

•Prescription, medicine and pharmacy-related services.

•Wellness, preventive-health, nutrition and care-management services.

•Digital health records, care plans, reports, prescriptions and care-coordination functionality.

•Customer support, complaints, feedback, surveys and service-quality interactions.

•Payments, subscriptions, memberships and transactions.

•Recruitment or professional/provider onboarding portals, where separately offered.

This Policy does not apply to websites, applications or services operated independently by third parties, except to

the extent CareYogi processes personal data in connection with those services or links to them from the Platform.

3. PRIVACY PRINCIPLES

CareYogi intends to process personal data in accordance with applicable law and the following principles:

•Purpose limitation – use data for identified and legitimate purposes.

•Data minimisation – collect and use data that is reasonably necessary for the relevant purpose.

•Transparency – provide understandable information about material processing activities.

•Accuracy – take reasonable steps to keep personal data accurate where it matters for the purpose of processing.

•Security – use reasonable technical and organisational safeguards appropriate to the risks.

•Accountability – maintain appropriate records, controls and processes for privacy and security obligations.

•Respect for individual rights – provide applicable mechanisms for access, correction, withdrawal of consent,

grievance and other statutory rights.

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 establishes obligations for Data Fiduciaries including reasonable

security safeguards, breach response, erasure subject to legal retention requirements, publication of contact

information for privacy queries and grievance redressal.

4. PERSONAL DATA WE MAY COLLECT

4.1 Identity and contact information

•Name and preferred name.

•Date of birth / age and, where relevant, sex or other information required for healthcare or service delivery.

•Mobile number, email address and communication preferences.

•Residential/service address and location needed for home visits or service delivery.

•Identity or verification information where required for authentication, safety, payment, legal compliance or

service delivery.

4.2 Healthcare and clinical information

•Symptoms, complaints, medical history, diagnoses and clinical observations.

•Allergies, medications, prescriptions and treatment history.

•Laboratory and diagnostic reports, imaging information and other investigation results.

•Vitals, measurements, device-generated health information and patient-reported information.

•Care plans, nursing notes, therapy notes, consultation notes and other records generated through services.

•Information concerning disability, pregnancy, family medical history or other health-related circumstances

where relevant to the service.

•Emergency-contact and caregiver information where provided.

Health information is treated by CareYogi as highly sensitive in operational and security design even though the

DPDP Act uses the broader concept of “personal data” rather than a separate statutory category of sensitive

personal data.

4.3 Account, transaction and service information

•Account credentials and authentication information.

•Bookings, appointments, subscriptions, service history and cancellations.

•Payment status, invoices, transaction references and billing information. Full payment-card details may be

processed by authorised payment providers rather than stored by CareYogi, depending on the payment method.

•Customer-support interactions, complaints, feedback and survey responses.

4.4 Technical and usage information

•IP address and network information.

•Device type, operating system, browser/application information and identifiers where applicable.

•Login, session, security and authentication logs.

•Approximate location or service-location information where needed for service delivery, fraud prevention or

security.

•Usage, navigation, performance and diagnostic information concerning the Platform.

•Cookies, SDKs and similar technologies, subject to applicable choices and settings.

4.5 Information provided by authorised persons and third parties

Personal data may be provided by an authorised representative, caregiver, family member, employer/organisation

arranging services, healthcare professional, hospital, clinic, laboratory, pharmacy, insurer/TPA, payment provider,

technology provider or other authorised source, where permitted or required for the relevant purpose.

Where another person provides information about a Patient, that person is responsible for having the authority

required to provide it.

5. HOW WE USE PERSONAL DATA

CareYogi may process personal data for the following purposes, depending on the service and applicable legal basis:

•Create and manage Customer and Patient accounts.

•Schedule, provide, coordinate and follow up on healthcare and related services.

•Facilitate teleconsultations, including identification, appointment management, communication and clinical

documentation.

•Facilitate home visits, nursing, caregiver, physiotherapy, diagnostics, pharmacy and other services.

•Create, maintain, retrieve and present digital health records and care information.

•Communicate appointments, reminders, prescriptions, reports, care instructions, service updates and safety

information.

•Process payments, subscriptions, refunds, invoices and financial records.

•Verify identity, provider credentials, eligibility, service access and account security.

•Detect, prevent and investigate fraud, abuse, security incidents, unauthorised access and other misuse.

•Provide customer support and handle complaints and grievances.

•Maintain, secure, troubleshoot and improve the Platform and its reliability.

•Conduct quality assurance, service analytics and operational reporting.

•Personalise or recommend relevant CareYogi services where permitted by law and subject to applicable

consent/choice requirements.

Send marketing or promotional communications where legally permitted and, where required, based on

appropriate consent or preference.

•Comply with applicable law, legal process, regulatory requirements and professional obligations.

•Protect the rights, safety and security of Patients, Customers, Healthcare Professionals, CareYogi and others.

•Establish, exercise or defend legal claims and maintain necessary business records.

•Conduct research, analytics or product improvement using de-identified or aggregated information where

reasonably possible and legally appropriate.

6. LEGAL BASIS / GROUNDS FOR PROCESSING

CareYogi will process personal data only where permitted under applicable law. Depending on the activity,

processing may be based on consent, certain legitimate uses or other lawful grounds recognised by applicable law.

Where processing is based on consent, CareYogi will seek consent through an appropriate affirmative mechanism

and will not treat acceptance of the general Customer Agreement as blanket consent to unrelated or optional

processing.

The DPDP Act requires consent to be free, specific, informed and unambiguous with clear affirmative action, and

permits processing for specified legitimate uses in defined circumstances. CareYogi's operational implementation

should be mapped to the final legal requirements and their applicable commencement dates. citeturn0search37

Healthcare services may also require separate clinical consent. The CareYogi Master Customer Agreement

specifically states that acceptance of that agreement is not intended to constitute blanket informed consent to every

future medical procedure. fileciteturn3file2L137-L150

7. HEALTHCARE RECORDS AND CLINICAL DATA

7.1 CareYogi may maintain digital health records associated with services delivered through the Platform, subject to

applicable law and the purposes described in this Policy.

7.2 Records may include consultation notes, prescriptions, reports, care plans, nursing/therapy documentation and

other information generated during service delivery.

7.3 Where a Healthcare Professional or Service Provider independently creates and maintains a clinical record, that

provider may have separate statutory and professional record-keeping obligations.

7.4 CareYogi will not use health information for unrelated commercial purposes merely because it is available

through the Platform.

7.5 Where data is used for analytics, product improvement or research, CareYogi should use de-identification,

aggregation or other privacy-enhancing measures where reasonably appropriate.

8. TELEMEDICINE, AUDIO/VIDEO AND COMMUNICATION DATA

8.1 Teleconsultation requires appropriate patient/RMP identification, mode of communication, consent, evaluation

and management in accordance with applicable telemedicine requirements. The Indian Telemedicine Practice

Guidelines identify consent as one of the elements to be considered before a telemedicine consultation.

8.2 CareYogi may process the minimum information reasonably necessary to schedule, authenticate, conduct,

document and support a teleconsultation.

8.3 Audio or video recordings of a consultation will not be treated as automatically authorised merely because the

consultation occurs by video or audio.

8.4 Where CareYogi proposes to record a consultation, it should obtain a separate, purpose-specific consent before

recording begins, identify the purpose and applicable retention period, and provide any legally required choice or

withdrawal mechanism.

8.5 Technical metadata, connection logs and security logs may be retained as necessary for service operation,

security, dispute resolution, compliance or other lawful purposes.

9. COOKIES, SDKs AND SIMILAR TECHNOLOGIES

CareYogi may use cookies, software development kits (SDKs), pixels, local storage and similar technologies to

operate the Platform, remember preferences, maintain sessions, measure performance, improve security and

understand usage.

Where required, optional analytics, advertising or similar technologies will be presented through an appropriate

consent or preference mechanism. The Platform should not make optional tracking a condition of receiving

healthcare services unless permitted by law and necessary for the stated service.

CareYogi should maintain a current Cookie/Tracking Inventory identifying each technology, provider, purpose, data

fields, retention and user choice mechanism.

10. HOW WE SHARE PERSONAL DATA

CareYogi may disclose or make personal data available to the following categories of recipients, where necessary and

permitted by law:

•Healthcare Professionals and Service Providers involved in the requested care.

•Hospitals, clinics, laboratories, diagnostic providers, pharmacies, therapists, home-care providers and other

healthcare partners.

•Caregivers, family members or authorised representatives where the Patient has authorised access or where

disclosure is otherwise permitted or required by law.

•Payment gateways, banks and payment service providers.

•Cloud hosting, database, communications, telemedicine, cybersecurity, customer-support and other technology

service providers acting on CareYogi's behalf.

•Professional advisers such as lawyers, auditors and insurers, where necessary.

•Government authorities, regulators, courts, law-enforcement agencies or other persons where required or

permitted by law.

•Corporate transaction counterparties in connection with a merger, acquisition, restructuring, financing or

transfer of business, subject to appropriate safeguards and applicable law.

•Other recipients where the Customer/Patient has specifically authorised the disclosure.

CareYogi should maintain a current data-sharing/vendor register and ensure appropriate contractual confidentiality,

security and data-processing obligations with relevant processors and service providers.

11. SERVICE PROVIDERS AND THEIR PRIVACY RESPONSIBILITIES

A Service Provider may receive health and service information necessary to provide care. The provider may also have

independent professional and legal obligations concerning the information it handles.

Where a provider operates an independent patient-record system or provides a service under its own privacy notice,

the Customer should review that notice where applicable.

CareYogi's role may differ by service. The Master Customer Agreement therefore identifies CareYogi as potentially

providing services directly or facilitating services through independent Service Providers.

12. INTERNATIONAL / CROSS-BORDER PROCESSING

CareYogi may use technology, cloud, communications or other service providers that process personal data outside

India, where permitted by applicable law and subject to applicable restrictions.

Before production, CareYogi should maintain an up-to-date data-flow map identifying where personal data is stored,

accessed or processed, including country, provider, purpose, data categories and applicable safeguards.

Cross-border processing will be managed in accordance with the DPDP Act, applicable rules, government

notifications and other laws applicable to the relevant processing activity.

13. DATA RETENTION

CareYogi will retain personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it was collected

or otherwise processed, subject to applicable legal, regulatory, professional, accounting, tax, contractual, dispute-

resolution and security requirements.

Because healthcare records may be subject to professional and legal retention obligations, deletion of a CareYogi

account will not necessarily result in immediate deletion of every healthcare record.

CareYogi should maintain a Data Retention Schedule identifying, for each category of data, the purpose, retention

period/criteria, legal basis and deletion/anonymisation method.

Where consent is withdrawn, CareYogi will stop processing based on that consent where required, while retaining

data where another lawful basis or legal obligation permits or requires retention.

14. DATA SECURITY

CareYogi will implement reasonable technical and organisational measures appropriate to the nature and risk of the

personal data processed. These may include:

•Encryption in transit and, where appropriate, at rest.

•Role-based and least-privilege access controls.

•Multi-factor authentication and secure authentication practices where appropriate.

•Logging, monitoring and audit controls.

•Secure backup, disaster recovery and business-continuity measures.

•Vulnerability management, patching and security testing.

Endpoint, network and application security controls.

•Vendor/security due diligence and contractual safeguards.

•Employee and contractor confidentiality and privacy training.

•Incident response and personal-data breach management procedures.

The DPDP Act requires Data Fiduciaries to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches

and contains obligations relating to breach intimation. citeturn0search37

15. PERSONAL DATA BREACHES

CareYogi will maintain an incident-response process for suspected or confirmed personal-data breaches.

Where a breach occurs, CareYogi will assess the incident and take the notifications, containment, remediation and

other actions required by applicable law and applicable regulatory directions.

The internal incident-response plan should define responsibilities for detection, triage, evidence preservation,

containment, risk assessment, regulatory notification, affected-person communication, remediation and post-

incident review.

16. YOUR PRIVACY RIGHTS AND CHOICES

Subject to applicable law and any applicable conditions or exceptions, a Data Principal may have rights including:

•Access information about personal data being processed and other information prescribed by law.

•Request correction, completion, updating or other permitted rectification of personal data.

•Withdraw consent where processing is based on consent.

•Request erasure where applicable, subject to legal and other permitted retention requirements.

•Use an authorised person or mechanism to exercise rights where permitted by law.

•Raise a grievance with CareYogi and, after using the prescribed internal mechanism where required, approach

the competent authority or Data Protection Board as applicable.

The DPDP Act expressly provides Data Principal rights concerning access, correction/erasure, grievance redressal and

nomination, subject to its terms and applicable rules. citeturn0search38

Requests may be submitted to: [privacy email / portal / address]. CareYogi will verify the requester as reasonably

necessary to protect Patient and Customer information and will respond within the period required by applicable

law.

17. WITHDRAWAL OF CONSENT

Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw consent through the mechanism provided by CareYogi or

by contacting the designated privacy contact, subject to applicable law.

Withdrawal does not affect processing that occurred lawfully before withdrawal. Withdrawal may also mean that

CareYogi cannot continue a service where the relevant data is necessary for that service and there is no other lawful

basis to process it.

Withdrawal of optional marketing consent should not ordinarily prevent access to healthcare services.

18. MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS

CareYogi may send service communications necessary to deliver requested services, such as appointment

confirmations, reminders, reports, prescriptions, payment notifications and care-related messages.

Promotional communications will be managed separately from essential service communications and will include an

appropriate unsubscribe or preference mechanism where required.

CareYogi should not use a patient's health condition, diagnosis or other health information to create targeted

marketing without a clearly established lawful basis and, where required, specific consent.

19. CHILDREN AND PERSONS REQUIRING A LAWFUL GUARDIAN

CareYogi may provide services to children and persons for whom a lawful guardian or authorised representative is

required.

Where applicable law requires verifiable parental or guardian consent before processing a child's personal data,

CareYogi will implement an appropriate verification mechanism.

The DPDP Act contains specific provisions concerning verifiable consent of a parent for processing a child's personal

data and consent of a lawful guardian for a person with disability in specified circumstances. citeturn0search37

CareYogi should configure age/guardian workflows before enabling child accounts or child-patient services and

should not rely solely on a generic adult-user checkbox.

20. FAMILY, CAREGIVER AND REPRESENTATIVE ACCESS

A Patient may authorise a family member, caregiver or other representative to access specified information or

manage selected services where CareYogi supports such functionality.

Access should be role-based and limited to the information and actions necessary for the authorised purpose.

CareYogi may restrict, suspend or revoke access where the authorisation expires, is withdrawn, appears invalid,

creates a security risk or is otherwise inconsistent with applicable law.

The Master Customer Agreement recognises family-member/caregiver access and states that access may be limited

by role, purpose or information category. fileciteturn3file4L313-L319

21. AI, AUTOMATION AND ANALYTICS

CareYogi may use software, algorithms, analytics and artificial-intelligence-enabled tools for administrative,

operational, support, documentation, scheduling, quality, fraud-prevention or care-support purposes where

appropriate.

Where an AI-enabled feature materially affects a healthcare decision, it should not replace the independent clinical

judgment of the responsible Healthcare Professional unless a lawful and clinically appropriate model expressly

permits that use.

CareYogi should identify AI-enabled processing in product documentation where it materially affects personal data,

and should apply appropriate human oversight, access controls, validation, monitoring and risk management.

CareYogi will not represent an automated output as a medical diagnosis or professional clinical opinion unless it has

been appropriately validated and presented within the applicable clinical and legal framework.

22. DE-IDENTIFIED, AGGREGATED AND STATISTICAL INFORMATION

CareYogi may create aggregated, statistical or de-identified information from data it processes where permitted by

law.

Such information may be used for service planning, quality improvement, research, analytics, product development,

reporting and other lawful purposes.

CareYogi should apply appropriate technical and organisational controls to reduce the risk that de-identified or

aggregated information can reasonably be re-identified.

23. DATA QUALITY AND CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITY

Customers and Patients should provide accurate and current information relevant to their care and services. The

Master Customer Agreement requires Customers to provide accurate and complete information reasonably relevant

to care. fileciteturn3file7L471-L498

CareYogi may provide mechanisms to correct account or profile information. Clinical corrections may also need to be

handled by the responsible Healthcare Professional or Service Provider in accordance with applicable record-keeping

requirements.

24. LINKS TO THIRD-PARTY SERVICES

The Platform may contain links, integrations or access to third-party services. Third-party services may have their

own privacy policies and terms. CareYogi is not responsible for privacy practices of third parties to the extent those

practices are outside CareYogi's control.

25. CHANGES TO THIS PRIVACY POLICY

CareYogi may update this Policy to reflect changes in services, technology, law or processing practices.

The revised version will show its effective date. If a change materially affects the manner in which personal data is

processed and applicable law requires notice or fresh consent, CareYogi will provide the required notice and obtain

consent where necessary.

The current version should remain accessible through the CareYogi Platform.

27. DATA PROTECTION OFFICER / SIGNIFICANT DATA FIDUCIARY

If CareYogi is notified or otherwise becomes subject to obligations applicable to a Significant Data Fiduciary, CareYogi

will appoint and publish the contact details of the Data Protection Officer and implement the additional governance,

audit, impact-assessment and other requirements applicable to that status.

The DPDP Act provides additional obligations for Significant Data Fiduciaries, including appointment of a Data

Protection Officer based in India, an independent data auditor and periodic impact assessments and audits.
